units.text: EXT. CORPORATE ROOFTOP - APIARY - MORNING
Above the thirty-first floor of Halcyon Dynamics, a sea of glass towers glitters in the sun.
Between the air-conditioning units and a ruined yoga mat, someone has set up six white beehives in a neat row.
Bees drift in lazy loops, indifferent to the quarterly earnings.
MARGOT FENWICK, 50s, Vice President of People Experience, glides across the gravel in a silk blouse and veil, as perfectly composed as a chess piece.
She carries a clipboard in one hand and a smoking tin in the other.
OSKAR LINDGREN, 40s, the company beekeeper, whose title on his badge is Chief Pollination Officer, adjusts a hive lid with a wooden tool.
Tall, rumpled, a beard going silver at the edges.
He moves slowly so the bees won't notice him.
PETRA IONESCU, 30s, Facilities, stands at the roof door with a walkie-talkie, glancing at her watch.
She wears hi-vis over a cardigan.
A NEW HIRE, 20s, steps out onto the gravel in a brand-new suit still creased from its packaging, a lanyard around his neck and a reusable cup of oat latte in his hand.
He squints at the hives and takes one hesitant step backward.
Ah, there he is. Our new Vice Assistant of Synergy.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Hi. I think there's a mistake. My badge says "Analyst."
units.name: NEW HIRE

units.text: Titles are fluid at Halcyon.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Don't make sudden movements, son.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: What kind of movements are sudden?
units.name: NEW HIRE

units.text: Most of them.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: He's here. No, he's fine. Yes, I'll tell him.
units.name: PETRA

units.text: Petra, thank you. You may go.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: I'd rather stay, actually.
units.name: PETRA

units.text: That was not a request.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Petra glares at Margot, lowers the walkie-talkie, and takes a slow, deliberate seat on an overturned bucket.
Today is your onboarding. At Halcyon we believe in rooting our people in something larger than themselves.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Like bees?
units.name: NEW HIRE

units.text: Like hives.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Like stings, mostly.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: He hands the New Hire a veil.
The young man puts it on, slightly crooked, the netting hanging in his eyes.
A single bee lands on his shoulder.
He freezes.
Is it going to--
units.name: NEW HIRE

units.text: It's just curious. Breathe out slowly.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: He does.
The bee lifts off.
Margot makes a note on the clipboard.
You handle pressure well. I'll mention that in your file.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: I haven't actually got a file yet.
units.name: NEW HIRE

units.text: Everyone has a file.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Everyone has two.
units.name: PETRA

units.text: Margot ignores her.
She approaches the nearest hive and lifts the lid with a flourish.
A hum rises, soft and grave.
This is the queen's chamber. You'll note the order. The discipline. The harmony of purpose. I like to think of our fifth-floor sales team in precisely this way.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: The sales team is not a queen.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: The sales team is a metaphor, Oskar.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: The sales team is a wasp's nest.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: Petra snorts.
Margot closes the lid a little harder than she means to.
Can I ask something?
units.name: NEW HIRE

units.text: Please.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Why bees?
units.name: NEW HIRE

units.text: A beat.
Margot looks at Oskar.
Oskar looks at the sky.
Petra studies her boots.
Margot's husband kept bees.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: Oskar.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: He died in March. She had the hives lifted here from the farm.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: That is private.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: It's rooftop. Nothing's private on a rooftop.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: For a moment, nobody speaks.
The wind lifts the edge of Margot's veil.
She smooths it with one hand, her fingers not quite steady.
Margot, the VP call.
units.name: PETRA

units.text: Yes. Of course.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: She hands the clipboard to the New Hire without ceremony.
Kwame. Welcome to Halcyon.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: You know my name?
units.name: KWAME

units.text: I read your file.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: I thought I didn't have one.
units.name: KWAME

units.text: Now you do.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: She sweeps toward the roof door, Petra a half-step behind her.
At the threshold she pauses, one hand on the frame, and speaks without turning.
Oskar. Teach him everything.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Everything about what?
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: Everything he'll need.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: She goes.
The door sighs shut.
Kwame lifts the veil from his eyes and looks at Oskar, who has already turned back to the hives.
Is she always like that?
units.name: KWAME

units.text: No. Sometimes she's worse.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: He hands Kwame the smoker.
It's warm and heavy, and a thin white thread curls from its spout.
Squeeze the bellows. Gently. Like you're asking a question.
units.name: OSKAR

units.text: Kwame squeezes.
The smoke drifts across the hive.
The humming softens, lowers, and one by one the bees settle into the quiet.
